CHIEF COMPLAINT
Evaluation of abnormal renal ultrasound with atrophic right kidney.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Ashley James is a 14-year-old previously healthy female who presented with acute onset right-sided abdominal pain and vomiting. She was initially evaluated and treated for a stomach virus with fluids provided, but symptoms significantly worsened the following day. Subsequent ultrasound imaging revealed an atrophic right kidney. Further imaging identified cysts on her kidneys and ovaries, swollen lymph nodes, and infection. She received evaluation in Jacksonville and subsequently in Atlanta where she was treated. Since treatment, she has had resolution of vomiting but continues to experience abdominal pain and burning sensations, particularly with eating and after consuming certain beverages. She reports occasional dysuria with difficulty initiating urination, noting that certain drinks like soda trigger burning sensation, and now restricts fluid intake to water and Gatorade. Parents note that at age 4, she had recurrent infections with multiple hospitalizations (3-4 times for approximately 3 days each) where she received fluids and antibiotics without definitive identification of infection source; these episodes subsequently resolved. Parents suspect a prior severe infection may have affected her kidney development. Patient denies hematuria. Currently reporting mild abdominal pain and burning sensation.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Abdominal pain and burning sensation, particularly associated with eating. Dysuria characterized by difficulty initiating urination and burning sensation triggered by certain beverages. Denies hematuria. Denies current nausea or vomiting. Otherwise well.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Atrophic right kidney. History of recurrent infections at age 4 requiring multiple hospitalizations. Evaluation by gastroenterology and genetics completed.

MEDICATIONS
Pepcid 40 mg daily. Claritin for allergies.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Significant for renal disease. Maternal grandfather had posterior urethral valves and obstructive neuropathy from birth, developed chronic kidney disease, was dialysis-dependent, had a renal transplant which subsequently failed, and died at age 47 from massive heart attack. Maternal great-aunt has end-stage renal disease, chronic kidney disease stage 5, diabetes, and hypertension (diagnosed in adulthood). Maternal cousins have kidney disease. Maternal grandmother has history of breast cancer.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient is active in softball and interested in joining drill team over summer.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
General: Well-appearing female, alert and oriented, sitting comfortably, not in acute distress.
Lungs: Clear to auscultation, sounds great.
Heart: Sounds great.
Remainder of exam: Within normal limits.

RESULTS
Renal ultrasound: Right kidney is atrophic. Left kidney appears enlarged, likely compensating for right kidney dysfunction. Genetic panel: No clinically significant mutations identified. Kidney function: Good. Blood pressure: Good.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
14-year-old female with atrophic right kidney and compensatory left kidney enlargement. Kidney function currently preserved. Patient at higher risk for future development of hypertension and proteinuria. Annual follow-up to include renal ultrasound to monitor kidney size and function, urinalysis to screen for proteinuria and hematuria, and blood pressure monitoring. Avoid non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs such as ibuprofen; use acetaminophen instead. Maintain adequate hydration with minimum 2 liters of water daily, particularly important during sports activities to prevent dehydration and strain on kidneys. Encourage continuation of healthy diet and active lifestyle. May follow up with primary care physician or adult nephrologist at local facility closer to home; does not need to travel for follow-up care.
